claims.text: Adding approximately 0.2 at.% yttrium to a high-entropy-alloy bond coat will enhance formation of a continuous alumina scale during cyclic oxidation.
Adding approximately 0.2 at.% yttrium will produce a denser alumina scale.
Adding approximately 0.2 at.% yttrium will improve alumina-scale adhesion.
The yttrium-induced alumina-scale changes will improve thermal-barrier-coating durability and reliability.
Undoped high-entropy-alloy bond coats such as CoCrFeNiAl typically form less-adherent oxide scales.
The less-adherent scales on undoped bond coats lead to spallation during high-temperature cycling.
Yttrium atoms will segregate to the metal–oxide interface.
The reactive-element effect of yttrium reduces oxygen-vacancy concentrations at the oxide growth front.
The reactive-element effect of yttrium hinders grain-boundary diffusion.
Reduced oxygen-vacancy concentrations and hindered grain-boundary diffusion promote a more uniform and adherent alumina scale.
A more uniform and adherent alumina scale resists spallation during thermal cycling.
Yttrium-doped bond coats will exhibit less oxide spallation than untreated bond coats.
Yttrium-doped bond coats will exhibit less crack initiation during thermal cycling than untreated bond coats.
Yttrium doping will extend the operational life of the thermal-barrier system relative to an untreated baseline.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during cyclic oxidation at 1100–1200 °C in oxidizing atmospheres representative of turbine operation.
Nonuniform yttrium distribution could impair the benefits of yttrium doping.
Formation of unwanted secondary phases could impair the benefits of yttrium doping.

contradictions.description: The boundary treats nonuniform yttrium distribution or secondary-phase formation as processing deviations outside the intended optimized intervention, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of either deviation as sufficient to falsify the hypothesis. Those observations could instead indicate failure to implement the intervention correctly.
